The conjugate variable of position is mo.why: The textbook conjugate pair, stated in Wikipedia and over 100 times verbatim.

sources.quote: The linear momentum of a particle is the derivative of its action with respect to its position.
sources.note: Listed as the first pair of conjugate variables in mechanics.

The SI unit of the quantity conjugate to.why: People say position and momentum are conjugate and that momentum is measured in kilogram metres per second, but nobody asks the unit of "the conjugate of position" as one fact; they would just say momentum.

The quantity conjugate to position is a.why: People say position and momentum are conjugate and that momentum is a vector, but nobody writes that the conjugate of position is a vector; they would name momentum directly.

sources.quote: Momentum is a vector quantity: it has both magnitude and direction.

The quantity conjugate to position is no.why: People say position and momentum are conjugate and that momentum is measured in kilogram metres per second, but nobody states what the conjugate of position is not measured in; they would name momentum directly and give its unit.

The quantity conjugate to position is co.why: 'momentum p' and 'energy E' are stated in every textbook and article, a short stock fact counted in the thousands in both corpora.

notes: Dev-split ABox revision (all determinate, no worlds): the conjugate variable of position becomes energy (conjugate_to, tagged symmetric and functional). Physics has few symmetric one-partner relations between named things; the conjugate pairs of quantum mechanics (position and momentum, energy and time) fit. Caveat: Wikipedia's Conjugate variables article also pairs time with frequency and position with wavenumber, the same pairs up to a constant; no query uses them. RELATIONS.md says energy and time are not a canonical pair, so no query uses that pair either. The one related question asks which letter symbol is conventionally used for the quantity conjugate to position (p before, E after): the stored fact is that momentum is denoted p, and the edit puts energy, denoted E, in momentum's place. Derived: the SI unit of the new conjugate and whether it is a vector or a scalar (compositions that look up a stored fact about energy), and whether it can be measured in joules (also a composition on energy's unit). The derived questions draw on two properties of energy (its unit, its being a scalar), the only properties of momentum and energy with a relation in RELATIONS.md; the symbol the related question asks has no catalogued relation. They differ in storage: the related fact is a sentence about momentum, the derived answers are worked out through the description 'the conjugate of position'. The near unrelated question asks the SI unit of momentum, which the edit does not touch.
